texts.preamble: Likki Vishwanath Reddy vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 19 June, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice P. Sree Sudha Writ Petition No.4629 Of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of Habeas Corpus directing the respondents to produce the detenu and to order for his release forthwith by declaring his detention vide proceedings No.01/PD-CELL/CCRB/RCKD/2023, dated 08.02.2023 passed by respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation order passed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.441 of General Administration (Special Law and Order) Department, dated 21.03.2023 as illegal. 3. Perusal of the impugned order of detention would reveal that Crime No.244 of 2022 of Pahadishareef Police Station was registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under Sections - 326, KL,J & PSS,J 504 and 148 read with 149 of IPC, while Crime No.1027 of 2022 of Uppal Police Station was registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 302, 201, 212, 506, 148 and 120B read with 149 and 109 of IPC and Section - 25 (1) (b) of the Indian Arms Act. 4. The allegations levelled against the detenu in Crime No.244 of 2022 are that on 17.04.2022 at about 16:00 hours, while the complainant, Mr. Yatham Suresh of Mamidipally Village, Balapur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, and others were present at BJP Office, meantime the detenu and accused No.3 were quarrelling with complainant for party issues and later they left from the place. After some time, while the complainant attending a function and standing outside function hall, the detenu, accused Nos.2 and 3 came there and picked up quarrel with the complainant and others and beat with iron rods. After completion of investigation, the Police filed charge sheet and the same was numbered as C.C. No.3709 of 2022, which is pending for trial. The incident occurred in this crime was on 17.04.2022, and after lapse of about ten (10) months, the order of detention was passed i.e., 08.02.2023. KL,J & PSS,J Likki Vishwanath Reddy vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148224257/ 1 5. Insofar as the second crime is concerned i.e., Crime No.1027 of 2022, the allegations levelled against the detenu along with his associates were living in a hostel nearer to the deceased house, and in furtherance of their plan, the detenu and his associates conspired together and attacked deceased No.1 (Narasimha Sharma) with hunting sickle and knives and when deceased No.2 (Srinivas, the son of the deceased No.1) came to rescue, they also attacked him and brutally killed both the deceased instantaneously. This incident is popularly known as 'double murder case'. In this case, the detenu is on bail. After completion of investigation, the police filed charge sheet on 10.01.2023 and the same is under P.T. vide C.C. No.3709 of 2022. 6. The incident in crime No.244 of 2022 had occurred on 17.04.2022, whereas, the order of detention was passed on 08.02.2023 after lapse of about ten (10) months. Therefore, the grounds referred to in the detention order are stale and not proximate KL,J & PSS,J to the order of detention.
texts.arguments: It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the aforesaid crimes registered against the detenu arise out of grudge and animosity between specific individuals and not public at large and that at the most the said crimes affect the maintenance of law and order, but not public order. There is also no rational nexus to the conclusions drawn in the detention order. 7. He would further submit that in view of the above, there only a solitary crime i.e., Crime No.1027 of 2022 of Uppal Police Station, wherein the detenu was granted bail. There is no allegation by the police that the detenu violated the bail conditions, nor filed any application for cancellation of bail. Thus, the order of detention under Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short 'Act, 1986'), has been passed and approved vide G.O.Rt.No.441, dated 21.03.2023 in a mechanical manner. 8. He would further submit that preventive detention of a person is an extreme measure resorted to by the State when ordinary KL,J & PSS,J criminal law is found not adequate to control his activities which cause disturbance to public order. In the case on hand, there is no disturbance caused to public order and it is would utmost disturb the maintenance of law and order. Thus, passing of order of detention by respondent No.2 based on solitary incident and the consequential confirmation passed by respondent No.1 is illegal and the same is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 9. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents would contend that the Detaining Authority having satisfied with the material available on record and considering the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed by the detenu passed the order of detention. He would further submit that two crimes have been registered against the detenu. The offences alleged against the detenu in Crime No.1027 of 2022 are punishable under Sections - 302, 201, 212, 506, 148, 120B read with 149 and 109 of IPC and also Section - 25 (1) (b) of the Arms Act, 1959. The offences committed by the detenu are grave in nature. The Detaining Authority considering that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences in future, which would again KL,J & PSS,J certainly affect the public order, issued detention order. Likki Vishwanath Reddy vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148224257/ 2 There is no error in it. 11. The Hon'ble Supreme Court held that this long lapse of time detention orders lose its significance because the said prejudicial conduct was not approximate in point of time and had no rational KL,J & PSS,J connection with the conclusion that the detention necessary for maintenance of public order and such a stale incident cannot be construed as justifiable ground for passing an Order of detention. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that detention order cannot be passed basing on solitary crime. 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration1 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. . (1982) 2 SCC 403 KL,J & PSS,J 14. In Sushanta Kumar Banik v. State of Tripura2, the Apex Court held that the preventive detention is a serious invasion of personal liberty and the normal methods open to a person charged with commission of any offence to disprove the charge or to prove his innocence at the trial are not available to the person preventively detained and, therefore, in prevention detention jurisprudence, whatever little safeguards the Constitution and the enactments authorizing such detention provide assume utmost importance and must be strictly adhered to. 15. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar3, the Apex Court held as under: Likki Vishwanath Reddy vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148224257/ 3 "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground . 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1333 . (1966) 1 SCR 709 KL,J & PSS,J that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order KL,J & PSS,J but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State." 16. Similar view was reiterated by the Apex Court in Arun Ghosh v. State of West Bengal4. 17. In Kanu Biswas v. State of W.B.5, the Apex Court relying on Ram Manohar Lohia3 noted that preventive detention can only be invoked in cases of breach of public order. The Court explained the difference between law and order and public order by stating that public order is said to be affected when the action of the detenu is in the nature of adversely affecting the even tempo of life of the community which causes a general disturbance of public tranquility. 18. In Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana6, the Apex Court held that a mere apprehension of a breach of law and order is not sufficient to meet the standard of adversely affecting the "maintenance of public order". Referring to the principle laid down by it in Ram Manohar Lohia3 and Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of . (1970) 1 SCC 98 (1972) 3 SCC 831 . 2022 SCC OnLine SC 424 KL,J & PSS,J Telangana7, the distinction between a disturbance to law and order and a disturbance to public order was discussed. 19. It was observed by the Apex Court that for the last five years, the Apex Court has [LEAKAGE_MASK] over five detention orders under the Telangana Act of 1986 for inter alia incorrectly applying the standard for maintenance of public order and relying on stale materials while passing the orders of detention. At least ten detention orders under the Telangana Act of 1986 have been [LEAKAGE_MASK] by the Likki Vishwanath Reddy vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148224257/ 4 Apex Court in the last one year itself. These numbers evince a callous exercise of the exceptional power of preventive detention by the detaining authorities and the respondent - State. 20. In Shaik Nazneen v. The State of Telangana8, the Apex Court [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order passed by the Division Bench of this Court confirming the detention order, approved by the State. In the said . (2021) 9 SCC 415 . 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 559 KL,J & PSS,J case, the said detention order was passed on the ground of detenu involving in four chain snatching cases. It was held that the State is not without a remedy, as in case the detenu is much a menace to the society as is being alleged, then the prosecution should seek for the cancellation of his bail and/or move an appeal to the Higher Court. 21. Referring to the observations made in Mallada K. Sri Ram6 and on examination of the facts of the case, the Apex Court held in paragraph No.12 which is as follows: "12. The reasons assigned by the authority in its detention, justifying the invocation of the provisions of the detention law are that the detenu has been granted bail in all the four cases and since he is likely to indulge in similar crime, hence the order of preventive detention." KL,J & PSS,J 22. The Apex Court and this Court time and again held that the detention orders shall be passed in rarest of rare cases and to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences which may disturb the public order. 23. In Adbul Sathar Ibrahim Manik v. Union of India9 relied upon by the learned Special Government Pleader, the Apex Court held as under: "The next submission is that there were no antecedents and that this being the solitary incident the detention is unwarranted. It is again a question of satisfaction of the detaining authority on the basis of the material placed before it. The authorities cannot and may not in every case salvage the antecedents but as noted above even a solitary incident may manifest the potentialities of a detenue in the activities of smuggling." Likki Vishwanath Reddy vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148224257/ 5 25. The Apex Court as well as this Court time and again held that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order".
